ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (latest revision in force), the Administrative Measures for Beneficial Ownership Information of Enterprises (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024), the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), the Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration of the People's Republic of China, and the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry of the jurisdiction in which the ultimate foreign investor is incorporated (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, ACRA, or equivalent competent registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path only: if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state, obtain an Apostille issued by that state's designated competent authority; do not add consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state, complete consular legalization through the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the PRC Embassy or Consulate in that state; do not add an Apostille. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the ultimate foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path only: Hague Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; consular legalization if it is a non-member; never both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate foreign investor, notarized by a notary public in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path only: Hague Apostille if the notarized resolution originates in an Apostille Convention member state; consular legalization if it originates in a non-member state; the two authentication methods are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document of the investor)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or Board of directors of the ultimate foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path only: Apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention for member-state issued documents; consular legalization through the foreign ministry and PRC consulate for non-member-state documents; never use both for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's principal relationship bank, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path only: the bank reference letter must be notarized, then either apostilled (if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state) or consular legalized (if the bank's jurisdiction is a non-member state); apostille and consular legalization cannot be used on the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and all PRC domestic lists and watchlists issued by the Ministry of Public Security, the People's Bank of China, and the competent Financial Intelligence Unit. All beneficial owners, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and ultimate natural-person controllers must be screened prior to incorporation and periodically thereafter. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence must be documented. Any sanction hit, PEP association, or unexplained beneficial ownership profile requires immediate suspension of formation, escalation to the AML compliance officer, and a Suspicious Transaction Report where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be composed of Standard Chinese characters; pinyin, English, or other foreign scripts cannot substitute for the registered Chinese name. The name must follow the four-tier statutory formula: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business-specific term, and organizational form (Limited Liability Company). A foreign-language translation or transliteration may be filed only as an auxiliary name after registration and may not independently carry on business. Use of China, Chinese, National, Central, or other state-related tokens is prohibited unless the competent ministry or SAMR approval is granted; transliterations of foreign trademarks must not create deception or conflict with recognized well-known marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, obtain the written SAMR rejection notice stating statutory and factual grounds. Within 30 days or the statutory appeal window, whichever applies, submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the upper-level market regulation administration, attaching the rejected name, corrected alternate name, and proof of pre-registration search. If reconsideration fails, file an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within six months of service of the reconsideration decision. Reapply concurrently with a modified four-tier name to preserve the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or address-only arrangement is rejected by PRC registration, tax, and banking authorities for a WFOE engaged in ghost-kitchen and virtual-brand delivery operations. The WFOE must maintain a physical, lease-backed office and commercial kitchen premises within the registered administrative jurisdiction. The food business license cannot be issued for a mailbox or virtual address; tax authorities will mark the taxpayer as abnormal and banks will refuse corporate account opening if operational substance cannot be established. The physical address must correspond to the food-business operational footprint, fire safety, food hygiene, and municipal zoning requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood, estimated 60-75 percent within the first 12 months for delivery-only cloud kitchens, because SAMR food-safety regulators, municipal tax offices, fire authorities, and market regulation inspectors conduct unannounced on-site visits. Checklist: (i) confirm physical presence and signage matching the registered Chinese name; (ii) verify food-preparation areas and sanitation controls; (iii) compare payroll, social-insurance, and invoices with actual operations; (iv) inspect fire-safety equipment and waste-disposal logs; (v) test delivery-brand order flow at the address; (vi) ensure the lease is not a mailbox or virtual office; and (vii) maintain on-site food business license display. Failure on any checkpoint can trigger abnormal-operation listing, license suspension, or tax closure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Zero statutory fee for initial beneficial ownership declaration under Order No. 3 (2024).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff by jurisdiction plus per-document Apostille fee of USD 20-65 or consular legalization fee; hard-copy courier and scanning included.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed translation firm or SAMR-approved translation service provider in China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per Chinese character or page, projected 30-60 pages of translated corporate records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 WFOE legal counsel and regulatory due-diligence fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese law firm licensed to practice in Mainland China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based fixed legal fee for WFOE incorporation advisory, name clearance, UBO filing, and AML/CFT screening; includes document review and regulatory opinions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 10, 12, 15, 20, 23, 26, 27, 28, 29, 32, 33, 35, 36, 42, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51 and 52; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 1, 2, 6, 11 and 15; Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (2021); Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2021), Articles 2, 4, 8 and 16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the municipal or district Market Supervision Administration where the registered office is located, acting through the national one-stop Market Entity Registration online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Registration Application Form together with the notarized or apostilled Articles of Association, filed as a Market Entity Registration through the SAMR online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the 2024 Company Law revision, no statutory minimum registered capital applies to a WFOE operating a delivery-only cloud kitchen, no paid-in capital verification report is required, and no blocked escrow or capital-verification account is mandated for this unrestricted industry. The shareholders are free to determine the subscribed capital in the Articles of Association, and actual contributions must comply with the agreed contribution schedule and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange capital-account admission rules when funds are remitted into China.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration portal under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-approval name search on the SAMR enterprise name portal using the proposed English and Chinese trade name. For a cloud-kitchen or virtual-brand company, the approved name should contain an industry element such as catering management, food service, or restaurant operation. The application must disclose that the investment is 100% foreign-owned, the business scope will cover delivery-only food preparation and multi-brand virtual restaurant operations, and the registered office address is in a commercially zoned building. The name reservation certificate is generated online after the SAMR nomenclature review, and the same certificate must be attached to the later incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name with English translation
Shareholder identity proof (passport or certificate of incorporation)
Proposed registered office address
Detailed business scope description
Name reservation application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, select a new distinctive name stem with a different industry suffix and re-file through the same portal; if rejection is based on prohibited terms, remove those terms and apply again; unresolved nomenclature disputes may be appealed to the SAMR name adjudication unit within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WFOE Incorporation Filing and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) municipal or district enterprise registration window or the one-stop online portal for foreign-invested companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign-Invested Company Registration Application through the SAMR consolidated window. Attach the notarized or apostilled Articles of Association, certificate of incorporation or passport of the sole foreign shareholder, the lease certificate for the registered office, the name reservation certificate, the appointment resolutions for the legal representative and first directors, the supervisor appointment, and the proof that the business scope does not fall within the Foreign Investment Negative List. The SAMR examiner will verify the company name, legal representative's identity, registered capital subscription, business scope and registered address, then issue the Business License and Unified Social Credit Code. The entire process is paperless in most cities and the registration is completed within five working days after the file is complete.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Company Registration Application Form
Notarized or apostilled Articles of Association
Shareholder certificate of incorporation or passport
Registered office lease certificate and property ownership proof
Appointment resolution for legal representative, director, supervisor and manager
Name reservation certificate
Business scope statement confirming no Negative List restriction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, SAMR will issue a rectification note; the applicant has 15 working days to cure missing signatures, notarization, lease defects or capital schedule ambiguities. If the Negative List issue is raised, the applicant may adjust the foreign shareholding or carve the restricted activity into a domestic subsidiary; after cure, the review queue is resumed without a new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Seals, Legal Representative Filing and Tax/Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) authorized seal engraving enterprise; local State Taxation Administration (STA) tax bureau; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, apply at a Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving enterprise to carve the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and contract seal; the engraving center reports the seal specification to the PSB electronically. Next, complete the automatic tax registration at the local State Taxation Administration office by filing the information on shareholders, directors, leasing expenses and the projected commencement date. Within 30 days of license issuance, register the company for social insurance and housing fund at the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau and the housing fund center. The legal representative must personally sign the company-file declaration and tax-payment method authorization.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copy
Legal representative identity document and appointment resolution
Seal engraving authorization and PSB filing form
Tax registration form
Social insurance registration form and initial employee roster
Housing fund registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal-filing data is incomplete, the PSB online seal database will display an error; the engraving center must resubmit the seal image set within one working day. If tax registration is not automatically completed, the taxpayer must attend the tax service hall in person with the business license and the legal representative identity; if the social insurance portal fails, file a correction note with employee registration and obtain a stamped acceptance slip.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Foreign Exchange Registration and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank with a foreign-exchange branch; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank direct-transfer mechanism
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a licensed commercial bank with a foreign-exchange branch and open the capital account together with the RMB basic deposit account. The bank will require the Business License, the Articles of Association, seal collection, legal representative identity, board resolution, and a completed Foreign Investor Information Form. After the account is opened, the bank submits the foreign exchange registration of the WFOE to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the direct-bank mechanism. The foreign shareholder then remits the subscribed capital to the capital account; the bank verifies the declared capital contribution purpose and enters the funds as paid-in capital. The funds may be used only for approved items such as lease, equipment, payroll, inventory and operating expenses, and each use must be supported by invoices and contract.
required_dossiers: Business License
Articles of Association
Company seal, financial seal and legal representative seal impressions
Legal representative identity document
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Foreign Investor Information Form
Capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening for AML/KYC concerns, submit a revised beneficial ownership declaration and provide board-resolved organizational chart; if SAFE direct registration is delayed, the bank will request additional explanatory documents on the use of funds; the applicant should amend the capital contribution schedule and resubmit within 5 working days; if the bank still refuses, choose another designated bank and re-open after obtaining the bank's written refusal reason.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operating, Environmental and Fire Safety Licensing for Delivery-Only Cloud Kitchen
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration for food business licensing; Municipal Fire Rescue Corps for fire acceptance; Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau for environmental registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the food business license application with the local Market Supervision Administration, using the delivery-only cloud kitchen category, and submit the floor plan, kitchen equipment list, fume purification system data, water supply and drainage schematic, staff hygiene files, waste-oil collection contract and food-safety management rules. Simultaneously, complete the environmental impact registration filing at the Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau through the national EIA registration portal, and file fire safety acceptance with the Fire Rescue Corps covering the fire alarm, emergency exits, automatic fire suppression, portable extinguishers, kitchen hood suppression system and structural load of the cooking equipment. Upon the initial municipal fire inspection, the Civil Defense clearance is recorded for the premises before food production commences.
required_dossiers: Food business license application form
Business License copy
Registered office property rights or lease certificate
Kitchen floor plan and equipment layout
Fume purification system specifications and maintenance contract
Waste cooking oil disposal contract with licensed collector
Food safety management rules and staff health certificates
Fire safety acceptance filing form
Environmental impact registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the food business license application is suspended, rectify the food-safety management plan, the kitchen zoning plan or the staff health certificate list within 10 working days and resubmit. If the fire inspection reports deficiencies, install or repair the required fire-suppression, alarm, exit-signage or emergency-lighting systems and apply for a re-inspection. If the environmental registration is incomplete, complete the online registration and upload the waste-oil contract and fume purifier maintenance records before starting operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (Food Business Licensing), Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau (EIA Registration), and Municipal Fire Rescue Corps / Emergency Management Bureau (Civil Defense and Occupational Clearance).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License for Catering Food Services and Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate for Appointed Gathering Premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau under the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Impact Registration Form (filing record) for a small or medium delivery-only cloud kitchen; full Environmental Impact Report is not required absent large-capacity central cooking or neighborhood-sensitive exhaust fume thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with GB 8978-1996 integrated wastewater discharge standard before municipal sewer connection, with pH 6-9, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, SS ≤ 400 mg/L, animal-vegetable oil ≤ 100 mg/L and ammonia nitrogen ≤ 45 mg/L; cooking fume: comply with GB 18483-2001, with fume concentration ≤ 2.0 mg/m³ and purification efficiency ≥ 60%; waste cooking oil must be collected in sealed containers by licensed waste-oil collectors and may not be discharged into storm drains; grease ducts must be cleaned according to the approved fire safety plan and fume purifier maintenance records must be kept on-site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Acceptance Filing or Certificate from the Fire Rescue Corps covering automatic fire alarm, fire-extinguishing equipment, kitchen hood suppression system, emergency exits, and structural load of installed cooking equipment; occupational disease and workplace safety registration with the Emergency Management Bureau; food-handler health certificates and legal food business compliance clearance before opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online services administered through the Electronic Tax Bureau portal (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the competent local branch tax bureau of the district where the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), the WFOE automatically receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as its Tax Identification Number. Through the integrated multi-certificate ('one-form, one-certificate') registration mechanism, the SAMR shares registration data with the STA, and tax registration is completed without a separate physical TIN certificate. The WFOE must then activate its Electronic Tax Bureau account, obtain its digital tax certificate/login credentials, complete the VAT taxpayer status filing (small-scale taxpayer or general VAT taxpayer), register payroll and individual income tax (IIT) withholding obligations, and file any non-resident withholding registrations for foreign shareholders. A non-resident enterprise without an establishment in China that earns PRC-source income is assigned a non-resident taxpayer identification number by the competent tax authority as part of withholding registration; a non-resident shareholder claiming treaty benefits must provide a tax residency certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not operate a check-the-box regime or hybrid-mismatch entity election mechanism; a WFOE is mandatorily classified as a Chinese tax-resident enterprise subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income. The only relevant election is indirect-tax status: a taxpayer with annual taxable turnover at or below CNY 5,000,000 may elect general VAT taxpayer status, while a taxpayer exceeding that threshold must be registered as a general VAT taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China, a unified national VAT with no sub-national sales tax; the applicable VAT rate for ghost-kitchen/catering and delivery-related food services is 6% (life services), while China's general standard VAT rate for goods is 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 0 for basic VAT/tax registration: every WFOE must be tax-registered immediately upon incorporation through the integrated SAMR/STA registration process. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. Below that threshold, the WFOE may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer (statutory simplified levy rate 3%, with no input VAT credit), or voluntarily elect general taxpayer status for full input VAT crediting.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates centralized electronic invoice clearance under the Golden Tax Phase IV system. All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-controlled e-invoicing infrastructure; the Fully Digitized Electronic Invoice regime requires each invoice to carry a unique invoice number, anti-counterfeit QR code, and digital signature, with real-time transmission to the STA. General VAT taxpayers issuing special VAT invoices and ordinary digital invoices must use the Electronic Tax Bureau portal or SAT-certified tax-control systems; no private or offline invoice issuance is permitted. For ghost-kitchen/delivery operations, consumer-facing settlement invoices and platform-based transaction documentation must also pass through the same centralized clearance and digital-stamping process.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from China customs territory are zero-rated where the title passes to an overseas buyer, the goods physically leave China under a customs export declaration, and the export foreign-exchange proceeds are received and reported through the SAFE trade monitoring system. Cross-border services are zero-rated or VAT-exempt only if they fall within the statutory 'cross-border taxable services' list under Caishui [2016] No. 36 and subsequent STA announcements, are supplied to a non-resident enterprise or individual, and are wholly consumed outside China. Domestic ghost-kitchen/delivery catering services, including food prepared and delivered in China, do not qualify for zero-rating because the place of supply is China. Qualifying separately identifiable offshore revenue, such as virtual-brand licensing or digital services supplied to a non-resident with no China-related use, may be zero-rated only when the legal, documentary, and foreign-exchange conditions are fully satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) with electronic customs-clearance release
Bill of Lading (or air waybill for air cargo) showing shipment from China to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt entry in the SAFE trade-monitoring system
Zero-rated commercial invoice and packing list
Underlying export sales contract, purchase order, or service agreement evidencing the cross-border transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs cross-match export declarations, logistics records, customs release data, and bank foreign-exchange receipts on a real-time basis. If zero-rating or export-tax-refund status is claimed without full substantiation, the STA will claw back the VAT refund and disallow any future zero-rating benefit, assess daily late-payment interest of 0.05%, and impose an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid. Fraudulent export or cross-border zero-rating claims are referred for criminal investigation under Criminal Law Article 204, exposing responsible persons to fines, confiscation of illegal gains, retroactive unlimited recovery periods, and imprisonment up to life imprisonment in severe cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi is classified as conditionally convertible on the current account, fully compliant with IMF Article VIII current account obligations since 1996, but subject to a non-convertible capital account regime administered by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. Under the Foreign Investment Law and its implementing regulations, foreign-invested enterprises, including WFOEs, are permitted full current account access for invoicing and trade settlement, while capital account transactions require a dedicated FDI foreign currency capital account registered with SAFE. The capital injection received in foreign currency must be credited to the capital account and converted into RMB within a compliance bank; conversions are governed by the 'real demand' principle and cannot be pre-hedged beyond the approved contract. Profit remittance by a WFOE is treated as a current account item after the audited annual accounts are prepared; the board must pass a distribution resolution, the entity must obtain tax payment receipts (including corporate income tax withholding certification for dividend distributions to the non-resident parent), and the local SAFE-branch licensed custodian bank will verify the authenticity of the distribution through the digital foreign exchange administration system. Hurdles include the absence of free floating convertibility, documentation-intensity of every conversion, and the requirement to use the SWIFT-cleared Chinese clearing system for repatriations rather than any unlicensed fintech lane.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE administration rules, export foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated into China within 180 days from the date of the export customs declaration; enterprises may apply to SAFE for an extension in justifiable commercial circumstances. Mandatory forced surrender of export proceeds to the state has been abolished since the 2012 reform; the statutory regime now imposes a 0% mandatory conversion ratio, meaning the ghost kitchen operating entity may elect to credit 100% of export proceeds to an RMB settlement account or retain them as foreign currency in an export foreign exchange settlement account. In practice, treasurers maintain retention balances below the Foreign Exchange Settlement Account upper-limit quotas and settle the majority of receipts to RMB to fund local payroll and supply chain costs. All proceeds must be tracked via the SAFE Plant Monitoring System and every credit must carry a valid trade purpose code from the current account trade catalogue.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account)
Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB Current Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Tax Payment Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign and domestic electronic money institutions such as Airwallex, Currenxie, PingPong and Payoneer do not hold banking licences capable of registering FDI capital accounts or performing SAFE-verified forex settlement. PBOC regulations require corporate entities receiving foreign exchange for capital account purposes to use a bank authorized by SAFE; hence EMIs are legally barred from servicing the core inbound and repatriation flows of a WFOE. Practically they retain marginal viability only for ancillary cross-border marketing procurement in small-value current account items, yet their service agreements with Chinese legal entities are subject to PBOC licensing scrutiny; therefore the treasury blueprint mandates primary settlement via licensed commercial banks and keeps EMI usage outside statutory treasury flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Chinese banking practice as codified by the PBOC client identification rules requires the legal representative (statutory director) to attend a personal KYC interview at the branch physically; remote video verification is accepted by a few national banks for the operational account but not for the FDI capital escrow account. A non-resident legal representative holding a foreign passport may delegate the interview to a mainland-appointed general manager provided a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney is produced; however, several provincial SAFE divisions still mandate one original-principal appearance. Where the director is outside China, banks with foreign branches such as Bank of China, ICBC and China Merchants Bank permit an interview at the overseas branch that is then teleconferenced into the mainland branch, satisfying the physical-presence rule, while consular proxy opening on a document-only basis is generally rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the offshore holding chain is multi-jurisdictional, and the ghost kitchen brand is a virtual trademark with no physical headquarters, creating a red flag for PEP/sanctions tracing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate registry certificates from every shareholder jurisdiction; complete ultimate beneficial owner declaration form (PBOC Form) certified by a licensed notary; sanctions and PEP screening reports from a recognized global database (Dow Jones / World-Check) stamped by the compliance officer of the legal representative; the parent board resolution appointing the local director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance: cloud kitchen delivery-only operations show heavy e-commerce inflows from UberEats and DoorDash that may be interpreted as cross-border digital money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The ISIC 5610 operating licence (Food Operation Permit), brand kitchen-dispatch lease contracts, real-time delivery platform settlement statements from UberEats and DoorDash, and a 12-month cash-flow projection prepared by the external CPA to demonstrate wage, utilities and ingredient procurement matching revenue patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI registered capital purpose mismatch: banks must reject capital inflows that fund unregistered business or repurchase (round-tripping) equity under Circular 638 / foreign exchange control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate (FDI-FECRS) conforming to the 2024 administrative measures; capital management statement approved by the domestic bank branch; intangible asset monetization not permitted as registered capital; a written undertaking by the board not to reinvest in securities or lend to affiliated parties without SAFE approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment receipt mismatch: the target payment rails (UberEats, DoorDash) are US-based; the KYC profile needs to evidence the commercial contract linking the China entity to the platform payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed operator agreements between the WFOE and the delivery platforms (or the local brand licensee), payout reconciliation statements from the platforms, cross-border e-commerce export filing / payment licence of the clearing PSP, and the foreign exchange purchase vouchers (Internal RMB conversion vouchers) issued by the processing bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection shall be executed by the overseas parent via SWIFT MT103 with the remittance fields explicitly tagged: Purpose Code 62012 (FDI capital injection/Investment) per the PBOC/SAFE current account catalogue; the beneficiary bank statement must reference the SAFE FDI registration number (or the 2024-standard FDI-FECRS). The beneficiary account is the dedicated Foreign Currency Capital Account (FCA) opened at the selected tier-1 bank; upon credit, the bank will require a written extraction application and a capital account use declaration (banking electronic verification) prior to conversion into RMB. The conversion must occur within the legal retention period, and a Chinese CPA performs capital verification producing the Capital Verification Report (investment verification) which the bank files to retain the 'paid-in capital' record. Any excess over the registered investment amount cannot be booked; application to SAFE for capital increase must precede subsequent dividend distributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational disbursements — ingredient procurement, cloud kitchen equipment, royalty payments to brand owners and cloud service subscriptions — the blueprint prefers SWIFT MT103 for ordinary supplier invoices, Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight 90-day confirmed) for large frozen food or equipment imports, and Documentary Collections for lower-risk recurring consignments. All payments require the corresponding current account filing / electronic trade verification with underlying invoices and contracts on the SAFE Plant system; Chinese outward remittance proposals in RMB above USD 50,000 must pass bank compliance sampling. Settlement intra-day railing via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) is recommended for renminbi flows within the Chinese ecosystem to reduce dependency on SWIFT, while the USD rails remain on CHIPS/Fedwire correspondent relationships with the U.S. delivery platforms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts (close-ended, real-demand basis) booked with the licensed custodian bank for the FDI equity conversions
FX swaps (foreign exchange swaps) for rolling short-term working capital without maturity extension beyond 1 year
FX options — plain-vanilla and risk-reversal structures — used only with documentary evidence of trade exposure

Cross-currency interest rate swaps permitted only against long-term offshore loans approved by SAFE, with NDFs strictly located offshore (Hong Kong/Singapore) and prohibited onshore as per PBOC circular limitations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Disclosure Report (data submitted to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System under the PRC Enterprise Information Disclosure Regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each calendar year for the immediately preceding reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the WFOE fails to publish its annual report by 30 June, SAMR must place it on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Business Operations within 10 working days after the deadline. Rectification can remove the listing, but failure for three consecutive years results in placement on the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, with cross-departmental joint punishment, restrictions on obtaining loans, investment, permits and licences, intensified supervision, and eventual administrative revocation of the licence or forced deregistration/strike-off. Fines for false, misleading or omitted disclosure range from RMB 10,000 to RMB 300,000, with additional liability for the directly responsible officer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (annual report for foreign-invested enterprises including actual controller and ownership structure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) in conjunction with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), filed through the integrated annual-report portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of each calendar year; any change in equity ownership, actual controller or foreign investor information must additionally be reported within 30 days after completion of the SAMR change registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing triggers a written correction notice. If the WFOE still does not correct within 20 working days, MOFCOM/SAMR may impose a fine of up to RMB 100,000 on the enterprise and up to RMB 30,000 on the directly responsible person. Repeated or serious violations become part of the public credit record and may block subsequent equity changes, capital increases or cross-border fund remittance filings, escalating to administrative restriction of business activities and potential licence revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Return (final annual CIT return and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (local competent tax authority under the jurisdiction of the WFOE registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the calendar year immediately following the close of the fiscal year (the CIT year in China is the calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, or RMB 20,000 to RMB 50,000 for serious non-filing; unpaid tax accrues a late-payment surcharge equal to 0.05% per day. Underpayment due to false returns, concealed income or under-reporting is treated as tax evasion, punishable by recovery of the unpaid tax, surcharge, and an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax evaded; deliberate evasion with large amounts may trigger criminal liability. Persistent non-compliance allows the tax authority to attach books, freeze bank accounts, forcibly collect the assessed tax and publicise the WFOE on the tax arrears public platform, though it does not itself automatically strike off the company; continued corporate delinquency in any mandatory filing chain may cause SAMR to revoke the licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual financial statement audit by a PRC-certified public accounting firm (audit report retained on file and available to regulators)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct annual filing fee or portal; the audited financial statements and audit report must be made available to SAMR, the tax authority and MOFCOM on request, and are used to support the SAMR annual report and the annual CIT settlement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By no later than 30 April is market practice for internal approval; in all events the audited accounts must be completed before the 31 May CIT settlement filing and before the 30 June SAMR annual report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A WFOE that fails to procure the required audit breaches the PRC Company Law accounting mandate. SAMR may demand rectification and refer the matter to the Ministry of Finance; the company faces correction orders and fines of up to RMB 100,000, with personal fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on directly responsible directors or supervisors. Unsigned or un-audited financial statements cannot lawfully support the tax settlement, and the annual report may be rejected as abnormal, ultimately exposing the company to the same abnormal-operations list and licence-revocation consequences in the first row.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, balance-sheet, asset or headcount threshold is available to exempt a Chinese WFOE. Under the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law, every limited liability company, regardless of size, must prepare statutory financial statements at the close of each fiscal year and have them independently audited by an accounting firm licensed in the People's Republic of China and signed by at least two certified public accountants. This is also a condition of the annual foreign-investment information report and of foreign exchange annual compliance in China. Even a loss-making ghost-kitchen WFOE with nil turnover is not excused from obtaining an audit report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CASBE / China GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS for the size-relevant provisions and are mandatory for WFOE financial statements; qualifying small and low-risk unlisted companies may elect the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but once IFRS/CASBE is used it must be applied consistently. The statutory audit is performed using the China Standards on Auditing (CSA), and taxable profit is separately reconciled to PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law in the annual CIT settlement return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PRC maintains no standalone public UBO register. Beneficial-ownership and actual-controller confirmation is achieved through (i) the annual Foreign Investment Information Report due by 30 June, which must disclose the full chain of investors up to the ultimate beneficial owner/actual controller; and (ii) the mandatory 30-day reporting change window under the Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting: any transfer of equity interest, increase or decrease of capital, change of actual controller, or amendment of the investor structure must be registered with SAMR and the change report submitted to MOFCOM within 30 days of the registration. For bank-account and AML purposes, the WFOE is also obliged to identify and confirm the beneficial owner of its corporate clients and counterparties under the PBOC beneficial-ownership identification regime; for its own ownership, the WFOE must keep an up-to-date internal beneficial-ownership and actual-controller ledger and produce it to PBOC, SAMR, tax or police authorities on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Officers
Register of Charges and Mortgages (if any encumbrances exist)
Minute Book containing shareholders' and board meeting resolutions
Share-Transfer Ledger and capital contribution record
Corporate seal usage and contract register
Accounting books and vouchers retention index

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,000 per year in most mainland cities, covering registered address maintenance and local compliance-agent services; higher in Beijing/Shanghai premium districts.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - USD 3,500 for a single WFOE ghost-kitchen/virtual-brand operating entity, with cost rising if multiple virtual brands are held under one WFOE, if intercompany transfer-pricing documentation is required, or if foreign-exchange and CIT complex schedules are added.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China applies a 25% statutory CIT rate to WFOE residents on worldwide income. A qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprise (taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, not more than 300 employees, and total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million) may access a 20% statutory reduced rate, with current policy relief producing an effective 5% rate for taxable income up to RMB 3 million for the 2023-2027 period. A WFOE obtaining High-Technology Enterprise certification may use a 15% rate. Additional R&D expenses are eligible for a 100% super-deduction, but no patent box or free-zone holiday is available for a delivery-only ghost kitchen.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Type) Form A100000 for resident enterprises, filed through the State Administration of Taxation's Electronic Tax Filing platform (e-Tax), with supporting schedules including A105000, A105050, A105080, A106000 and A107012.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus quarterly provisional returns; quarterly CIT prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each calendar quarter; VAT is filed monthly or quarterly as registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed and final tax settled by 31 May of the next calendar year following the fiscal year-end, i.e. within five months; quarterly CIT prepayments are due within 15 days of each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the WFOE's gross turnover from ghost kitchen delivery operations, including all receipts from UberEats, DoorDash, self-delivery and app-based virtual-brand sales, net of discounts and returns, excluding VAT and consumption tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every sales payout must reconcile with platform settlement statements and Chinese bank/PSP records. Do not net out royalty fees owed to the foreign brand owner; deduct such fees as expenses only if supported by a valid contract, arm's length pricing and WHT repatriation filings. Revenue from overseas platform servers is still China-source and taxable if the ghost kitchen operates and fulfils in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct food ingredient costs, cloud-kitchen lease rent, kitchen labour, disposable packaging, delivery rider costs for in-house riders, and utility costs directly attributable to food production.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory valuation must follow actual-cost methods; related-party purchases from the foreign parent or sourcing affiliates must use the comparable uncontrolled price or comparable data. Transfer-pricing adjustments in cost allocation must be reflected in the annual CIT reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-income taxes deductible before CIT, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, property tax, land-use tax and similar levies tied to operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIT itself and VAT do not belong on this line. Property taxes on the kitchen property must be declared by the WFOE as the user or lessee; if the property is owned by an offshore related party, the lease rental must be at arm's length and subject to non-resident rental income WHT of 10% of gross rent unless DTA relief applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Delivery platform commissions, online advertising, coupon promotions, menu branding costs, and sales staff payroll.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entertainment expenses are deductible only up to 60% of the actual amount and are limited to 5% of operating revenue; advertising and promotion expenses are deductible at 15% of revenue (30% for special industries), with any excess carried forward. Payments to foreign delivery platforms for software or listing services must be scrutinised for non-resident service WHT at 10% or applicable treaty rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management salaries, office rent, accounting and legal fees, insurance, depreciation, amortisation, bank charges, and head-office management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Employee welfare costs are capped at 14% of total wages, union expenses at 2%, and education funds at 8%; management fees charged by the foreign parent are deductible only when the services are actually rendered and the fee is arm's length and supported by contemporaneous evidence. Otherwise they are treated as profit distributions and subject to dividend WHT upon adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense, exchange losses, financial handling fees, and related-party borrowing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The thin-capitalisation rule restricts interest deductions for excess related-party borrowing; the debt-to-equity ratio is generally 2:1 for non-financial enterprises. Interest paid to a non-resident parent is subject to 10% WHT (or 7% under the Mainland-Hong Kong arrangement if eligible), and the rate must reflect arm's length borrowing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as operating revenue less operating costs, taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses and financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any manipulation of the profit margin before TP documentation will attract comparability adjustment. The WFOE should benchmark its net profit using the Transactional Net Margin Method against comparable unrisked contract restaurants or cloud-kitchen operators.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit adjusted for non-operating income such as government subsidies, penalty receipts and disposal gains, and non-operating expenses such as donations, fines and asset losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fines and penalties are non-deductible; charitable donations are deductible only when made through approved channels and are subject to a 12% of total annual profit cap. Local government subsidies not linked to asset purchases are generally taxable; subsidies earmarked for equipment purchases may be deferred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses, deduct tax-exempt income, and adjust for foreign exchange, depreciation, amortisation, asset losses, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A loss offset is allowed only for China-source losses within five years; a high-technology WFOE may use a ten-year period. Foreign parent guarantee fees or cross-border cost-contribution arrangements not meeting arm's length standards must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 (Box 10) - Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals reconciled accounting profit; tax payable equals taxable income times 25% or the applicable preferential rate, less foreign tax credits, R&D super-deduction credits, and quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If profits are to be distributed to a foreign shareholder, the annual return position must be consistent with the eventual outbound dividend WHT base. A failure to book TP adjustments may cause the tax authority to reclassify remittances as dividends and assess 10% WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return triggers a penalty under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law: up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious non-filing. Under Article 32, a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% runs on unpaid tax until payment. Under Article 63, deliberate tax evasion is penalised at 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal tax fraud under Criminal Law Article 201 can result in imprisonment of up to seven years in aggravated circumstances; false fapiao issuance under Criminal Law Article 205 carries additional criminal monetary fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by the WFOE to foreign enterprise shareholders under CIT Law Articles 3(3) and 37; 20% IIT withholding applies to dividends paid to foreign individual shareholders unless a treaty provides a lower rate. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong tax arrangement, a 5% DTA rate applies to enterprise beneficial owners holding at least 25% of the shares for the period preceding distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA reduced withholding, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home jurisdiction and deliver it, together with a Beneficial Ownership Statement and shareholding proof, to the WFOE withholding agent. The WFOE files the non-resident enterprise withholding return and remits WHT within seven days of dividend payment. Under STA Announcement No. 60 (2015), the non-resident can apply treaty treatment before formal approval if the substantive documentation is supplied, but the tax authority may deny relief if the shareholder is only a conduit, lacks economic activity, or does not have control over the dividends. The WFOE must retain the TRC, board minutes, share registry, bank settlement proof and substance documentation to support the reduced rate in an audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% of the gross amount. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong arrangement, interest may be reduced to 7% for qualifying beneficial owners and royalties to 5% for certain approved copyright or industrial royalty income; other DTA rates commonly range from 5% to 10%. Payments for brand licence fees from the ghost kitchen's virtual brands to a related foreign parent must pass the beneficial-ownership test; excessive royalties may be recharacterised as dividends and subject to 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory if annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property or financial asset transfers, or RMB 100 million for receipt or payment of services. Master File preparation is mandatory where the consolidated group annual related-party revenue exceeds RMB 1 billion. China also requires the annual related-party transaction disclosure form to be filed with the CIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China has no formal Economic Substance Regulation but applies the general anti-abuse rule under CIT Law Article 47 and the substance-over-form principle. For a ghost-kitchen WFOE, minimum economic substance requires a real leased kitchen, kitchen employees, payroll, delivery platform contracts, revenue settlement in China, risk control and strategic management. If the WFOE is a mere shell, tax authorities may refuse treaty benefits, deny expense deductions, or impose withholding on deemed dividends. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must be located in China and supported by board meetings, employment contracts and operating records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Unreported Digital Platform Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The ghost-kitchen WFOE downloads daily sales reports from UberEats and DoorDash but instructs the settlement bank or PSP to pay a portion of gross food sales to a personal bank account or an offshore nominee, thereby under-declaring operating revenue in the annual CIT return and avoiding VAT and CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 63 (Tax Administration Law) imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05%; Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal liability for tax evasion on top of tax penalties. For VAT false-invoicing, Criminal Law Article 205 may apply with monetary fines equal to the falsely-issued invoice amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for restitution of the diverted revenue, unpaid taxes and related surcharges. Directors may be placed on the tax-related blacklist, barred from leaving China, deprived of personal assets, and sentenced to up to seven years' imprisonment for aggravated evasion. Corporate bank accounts and delivery platform accounts will be frozen.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell/Conduit WFOE and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is registered with no physical kitchen and zero operational staff; all brand strategy, supply procurement and delivery app management are conducted from the foreign parent's offshore office; the WFOE's only commercial activity is collecting customer revenue, paying a 90% brand royalty offshore, and remitting the residual to shareholders under treaty-reduced WHT as dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CIT Law Article 47 (general anti-abuse rule) and Article 48, the tax authority may recharacterise the structure, deny the royalty deduction, deem the profit remittance as taxable dividends, assess underpaid tax, and impose special tax adjustment interest. Treaty benefits may be denied and the full statutory 10% dividend WHT with penalties may be applied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false substance declarations or filed shell annual returns may be personally liable under civil fraud principles, ordered to restore diverted assets, placed on the 'serious dishonest person' list with travel and banking restrictions, and if the shell was used to obtain tax refunds or export rebates, criminally prosecuted and imprisoned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and TP Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE enters into service agreements with a foreign parent that lack comparability, calculates brand royalties at 15% of gross revenue when independent ghost kitchen chains operate at 3-5%, and pays interest on shareholder loans at 12% when the market rate is 4%. When required by the tax authority, the WFOE fails to produce a Local File where aggregate related-party service transactions exceed RMB 100 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 41 requires arm's length pricing; Article 44 allows the tax authority to determine taxable income based on available comparable data if TP documentation is not produced; Article 48 imposes special tax adjustment interest on additional tax. Penalties under Article 63 may reach 50% to 500% for fraudulent underpayment, and a criminal referral under Criminal Law Article 201 is possible if the mispricing is deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved inflated management fees and signed inaccurate TP files may be personally liable for the additional tax, interest and penalties if the company is insolvent due to profit stripping. They may be blacklisted as defaulters, have personal property attached, and face criminal prosecution for abetting tax evasion, with imprisonment of up to seven years.
